name: MonarchPostCard
title: PostCard
wrapsNative: MonarchCard (androidx.compose.material3.Surface) with androidx.compose.foundation.clickable, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow, MonarchAvatar and MonarchBadge; android.text.format.DateUtils for the relative time
summary: A post in a community feed or search result: author, relative time, pinned and answered markers, tags, title, a short excerpt, and reaction and comment counts.
whenToUse: In a community feed, a forum list or search results, where each post opens its own screen.
whenNotToUse: Not for a chat message; use the conversation's message bubble. Not for a link preview; use MonarchLinkCard.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchPostCard(title: String, author: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, pinned: Boolean = false, answered: Boolean = false, authorImage: Painter? = null, excerpt: String? = null, excerptLength: Int = 220, publishedAt: Long? = null, now: Long? = null, tags: List<MonarchPostCardTag> = emptyList(), reactionCount: Int? = null, commentCount: Int? = null, labels: MonarchPostCardLabels = MonarchPostCardLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null)
public class MonarchPostCardTag(label: String, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral)
public class MonarchPostCardLabels(pinned: String? = null, answered: String? = null, reactions: ((Int) -> String)? = null, comments: ((Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: onClick
options.description: Opens the post; the app navigates.

options.name: authorImage
options.description: The author's picture, loaded by the app. null shows initials.

options.name: excerpt
options.description: The plain-text body, shortened at a word boundary. Empty after trimming is not shown.

options.name: excerptLength
options.description: The longest excerpt shown, in characters, before the ellipsis.

options.name: publishedAt
options.description: When it was published, in epoch milliseconds (UTC), shown as "3 hours ago".

options.name: now
options.description: The current time for the relative time, for tests. null uses the clock, refreshed every minute.

options.name: tags
options.description: Badges after the author line: category, topic or status.

options.name: reactionCount
options.description: "12 reactions" in the footer; null hides it, zero is shown.

options.name: commentCount
options.description: "4 comments" in the footer; null hides it, zero is shown.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The interaction source of the card's button.

options.name: actions
options.description: Controls at the end of the footer, such as a bookmark button. They are separate buttons.

states.name: default
states.description: Author line, title, and the excerpt and counts when given.

states.name: answered
states.description: A success badge "Answered" in the author line.

states.name: pressed
states.description: A ripple over the author line, title and excerpt, and the focus ring when focused from a keyboard.

appearance: A MonarchCard on the surface color with its default border and 12dp corners; the title in the default text color, the author line, excerpt and counts in the muted text color, and badges in their tones' subtle colors. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web card is an article whose title is a link with an href and an optional renderLink; on Android, as on iOS, the author line, title and excerpt are one button that calls onClick, and the app navigates. The heading level option has no meaning on Android. The time uses DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString in the device's locale instead of the web's RelativeTime. The web draws thumbs-up, comment and pin glyphs before the counts; Monarch bundles no icons, so the counts are written in full ("12 reactions · 4 comments") and pinned is the word. Footer actions are separate buttons, never nested in the card's button.
accessibility: The author line, title and excerpt are one button that TalkBack reads in order: author, time, pinned, answered, tags, title, excerpt.
The counts are one element read as "12 reactions, 4 comments"; the dot between them is hidden.
The answered state is a badge with text and pinned is a word, so neither depends on color.
Footer actions keep their own names and roles and are reached after the card's button.
All text wraps and grows with the font size setting; the button area is far above 48dp.
edgeCases: An excerpt that is empty after trimming is not shown.
A single word longer than the cut is cut at the limit.
Counts of zero are shown; pass null to hide a count.
Large counts use the locale's grouping, such as 1,204.
Many tags wrap onto new lines.

examples.title: Post
examples.template:
MonarchPostCard(
    title = {{title}},
    author = {{author}},
    onClick = { /* Open the post. */ },
    answered = {{answered}},
    excerpt = {{excerpt}},
    publishedAt = {{publishedAt|millis}},
    now = {{now|millis}},
    tags = listOf(MonarchPostCardTag({{tags.0.label}}), MonarchPostCardTag({{tags.1.label}})),
    reactionCount = {{reactionCount}},
    commentCount = {{commentCount}},
)
examples.code:
MonarchPostCard(
    title = "How do you plan your week?",
    author = "Sam Lee",
    onClick = { /* Open the post. */ },
    answered = true,
    excerpt = "I keep a short list every Monday and review it on Friday. Curious what works for others, especially with a lot of meetings.",
    publishedAt = 1_778_403_600_000L,
    now = 1_778_414_400_000L,
    tags = listOf(MonarchPostCardTag("Questions"), MonarchPostCardTag("Planning")),
    reactionCount = 12,
    commentCount = 8,
)

examples.title: With a save button in the footer
examples.code:
MonarchPostCard(
    title = "Release notes for March",
    author = "Ben Okafor",
    onClick = {},
    pinned = true,
    commentCount = 0,
    actions = {
        MonarchButton(
            text = if (saved) "Saved" else "Save",
            onClick = { saved = !saved },
            variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost,
            size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm,
        )
    },
)
